title: Normalization comparison objects on the isomorphism locus
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, ℓ any natural number, ν:X′→X a finite morphism of schemes, and V an open of X such that ν restricted over V is an isomorphism. Let j:U→X and j′:U′→X′ be open immersions with ν′:U′→U giving a Cartesian square j′ν = ν′j. Set R = Λ/(ℓ). Then V^*(j_! R_U) and V^*(ν_*j′_!R_U′) are isomorphic as Λ-module sheaves, using inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], and direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. No comparison morphism is specified.

source.place: Proof sketch: cokernel constructibility and vanishing over the isomorphism locus; arbitrary-mono generalization justified by finite stalks

proof.text: Apply extension-by-zero base change to the given Cartesian square. Pullback of the constant coefficient sheaf along ν′ is constant, so obtain an isomorphism e: ν^*(j_!R_U) ≅ j′_!R_U′.

Let W = ν⁻¹(V) and r = ν restricted to V. Its square with W→X′ and V→X is Cartesian. The composition isomorphisms for inverse image identify r^* V^*(j_!R_U) with W^* ν^*(j_!R_U). Apply W^* to e, obtaining er: r^* V^*(j_!R_U) ≅ W^*(j′_!R_U′).

Open (hence étale) base change identifies V^* ν_*(j′_!R_U′) with r_* W^*(j′_!R_U′). Use the module-valued source theorem Etale.isIso_baseChangeMap_flip_of_isPullback on the flipped restriction square; this is the restriction exchange identification of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-underived-exchange-restriction]. Since r is an isomorphism, its inverse-image functor has inverse (r⁻¹)^* by the identity and composition isomorphisms. Its right adjoint r_* is consequently an equivalence, and the unit id→r_*r^* is invertible. Compose this unit on V^*(j_!R_U), r_*er, and the inverse open base-change isomorphism. No auxiliary Cartesian square on U or U′ is necessary; the argument also applies to empty opens and zero coefficients. Finiteness of ν is not used, but its existing hypothesis is preserved.

proof_origin.place: Identification over the isomorphism locus, assembled from extension-by-zero base change on the original square, restricted inverse-image composition, and open base change; Lean proof by X2, second reading 2026-10-14.
